title: References Basics
code:
def modify(number):
    number = 10
    print("Number in modify function is:", number)

def main():
    number = 5
    modify(number)
    print("In main function, number is still:", number)
 
main()

lines.explanation: defining a function called 'modify' which takes in an integer argument 'number'

Assigning the value '10' to the variable 'number'. Note that th variabe 'number' is the local variable and its scope is only confined to this function. What we do here is modify the value of the variable 'number' instead of the using the one that is passed as the argument

lines.code: print("Number in modify function is:", number)
lines.explanation: Printing out the number in the modify function
defining the variable 'number'. This is not same as the number variable defined above. Again this variable's scope is only confined to this function and hence it is an example of a local variable.
now we cll the modify function within the main function and passing the value of number as '5'.

lines.code: print("In main function, number is still:", number)
lines.explanation: In the main function the value of variable 'number' is still '5'
